name: Capitol Reef National Park
blurb: Pinyon-juniper slopes, bighorn and deer, and the cougars that hunt them.

tip.title: Remove the mountain lions
tip.text: Cougars are the main hunters of deer and bighorn here. Set Mountain lion to -100% and watch mule deer, then the shrubs they browse.

sources.title: National Park Service: Capitol Reef nature

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Capitol Reef National Park, Mule deer, Pinyon–juniper woodland). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives plant growth, though heat and dryness limit how much of it plants can use.

nodes.name: Two-needle pinyon
nodes.desc: A small pine of the dry woodlands, with large seeds eaten by birds and rodents. Drought and insects can kill stands.
Grows with pinyon in the pinyon-juniper woodland that covers much of the Colorado Plateau.
A low, spiny cactus that stores water in its pads. Bighorn sheep break open cacti when grass is scarce.
A native bunchgrass of sandy soils on the Colorado Plateau, grazed by hoofed animals.
A browser that eats mostly shrubs and trees, with some forbs, grass and fruit. Coyotes and cougars hunt it.
Lives on steep rocky ground. Eats mainly grass, switching to cacti and forbs when grass is scarce. Cougars, coyotes and bobcats prey on it.
The most-recorded mammal near the park. A small seed-eating rodent that many snakes, scavengers and canids eat.
A crow-family bird that harvests pine seeds and caches them, so it helps spread pines.
An omnivorous ground squirrel active in desert heat. GloBI records show it eating mice.
A large constrictor that hunts rodents, ground squirrels and birds.

nodes.name: Great Basin rattlesnake
nodes.desc: A pit viper that ambushes rodents and lizards on rocky slopes.
A clever omnivore and scavenger, the most-recorded bird near the park.
Soars over the canyons and feeds mainly on carrion, finding it by smell.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The main large predator of deer and bighorn in the canyon country.
An adaptable hunter of rodents and young deer that also eats carrion.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the thin desert soil.

story: Capitol Reef in south-central Utah is about 60 miles long and only 6 miles wide. It protects most of the Waterpocket Fold, a nearly 100-mile rocky spine and a warp in the Earth's crust 65 million years old. It is named for white sandstone cliffs with domes like those on capitol buildings.
matters: Locally, a "reef" is any rocky barrier to land travel, as ocean reefs are barriers to sea travel. The area became a national monument in 1937 and a national park in 1971.
